basic_info:
: A 4-year-old boy, second child of healthy non-consanguineous parents, born at term from uneventful pregnancy. Birth weight 3.010 kg, no perinatal suffering (APGAR score 8–9). Psychomotor development normal during first 2 years except altered sleep-wake rhythm. Language regression at 2–2.6 years, social regression at about 3 years, lack of direct eye contact in interactive games. Cognitive development within normal range (Nonverbal IQ = 93). Hyperactivity, limited eye contact, motor and vocal stereotypies, severe impairments in language and communication, fecal incontinence due to lack of sphincter control. Facial dysmorphism without congenital malformations reported. No family history or social history detailed. No risk factors explicitly mentioned.

Patient

: A 4-year-old girl, born at term by caesarean section from non-consanguineous healthy parents after uneventful pregnancy. Birth weight 2.2 kg, no perinatal suffering (APGAR score 8–9). Psychomotor development delay with significant impairment in acquisition and use of language. Developmental

: trunk control at 8 months, standing at 18 months, autonomous walking at 30 months, lack of sphincter control at 36 months. At age 3 years underwent inguinal hernia surgery. Clinical evaluation at 36 months revealed neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by expressive language impairment, motor coordination deficit; flat foot and knee valgus noted. Mild dysmorphic

: slightly upslanting palpebral fissures, relatively low-set protruding ears with prominent lobes, hypoplastic alae nasi with depressed nasal tip. No congenital malformations. Audiological exam showed no hearing problems though scared by loud noises. Able to perform and imitate simple motor movements but difficulty with imitation of movement sequences. Attention deficit with inability to stay focused for more than 15–20 minutes on specific activity. Discomfort in socializing with peers, partially improved after starting primary school. No family history or social history detailed. No risk factors explicitly mentioned.

examination.exam_items: a-CGH analysis, Real-time PCR experiments, clinical evaluation including physical examination, audiological examination, cognitive assessment (Nonverbal IQ), psychomotor developmental assessment, observation of behavioral features (eye contact, stereotypies, hyperactivity), assessment of sphincter control, evaluation of dysmorphic traits.
examination.exam_results:
: a-CGH showed microduplication in 7p22.2 region spanning 371.165 kb (positions 3074785 to 3445950) and microduplication in 12q13.3 region spanning 345.669 kb (positions 56670637 to 57016306). Real-time PCR confirmed both CNVs. Both CNVs classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS) per ACMG. Cognitive development NVIQ = 93. No congenital malformations. Facial dysmorphism noted. No further chromosomal analyses or segregation analysis performed.
